propositions: The retired trigger word 'recheck-review' collides with external CI's substring-based comment matcher mapping 'recheck = verify', causing unintended CI workflow dispatch and run cancellations when the bot's own reply texts embed the retired word.

The new trigger token 'rerun-llm-review' was chosen to avoid substring overlap with any ini-mapped comment-added key, and handler logic was restructured to post a descriptive refusal for retired-word comments while never queuing a review or writing a label.

All bot-posted reply texts (_ACCEPTED_MESSAGE, findings refusal, retired-word refusal) must be scrubbed of ini-mapped trigger words to prevent the bot's own comments from re-dispatching the CI workflow.

The retired word survives only in retrigger.py (detector regex and module docstring) and test_review_bot_retrigger.py (refusal branch exercise), with all contributor documentation and guides updated to the new word.

Tests parse infra/gerrit/gerrit_to_platform.ini.template at runtime to assert substring-safety in both directions and verify no posted reply contains mapped words, catching future CI mapping collisions in test rather than production.
The change implements hard cutover with no deprecation window, since keeping the old word alive preserves the CI collision risk.
